bounds.domain: One reviewed telephony proposal, one fixed authenticated owner/session/device/operation/digest, one execution claim and one renderer attempt. Capability may be absent. Foreground loss, cancellation and selection/request invalidation each occur at most once; at most one native invocation and one exact result are admitted.
bounds.projection: The TS coordinator reserves its journal before decision and claim, marks applying before invocation, and checks the renderer guard at each awaited admission boundary. Successful/failed/unknown native results are symbolic classes admitted by the production closed validators. A contradictory result is not published as success. Cancellation before dispatch fences invocation; cancellation after an admitted invocation does not undo its known result. Receipt upload can retry a terminal journal without invoking the native port again.
bounds.currentRequestBoundary: Selection validity combines the reviewed context key and host-supplied current-request proof. The stricter selected-item binding requires an external host to enable currentRequestTelephonyPolicy and provide a valid proof. No in-tree host currently enables that option. This model does not prove native selected-item identity or foreground state from a renderer assertion.
bounds.conformance: Mandatory tests execute the real shared DeviceActionCoordinator over controlled authenticated-transport, journal and native-executor ports, and the actual telephony operation/result validators. Every named test in both suites must execute and pass with no skipped/todo tests; receipts bind model, cases, source hashes and concrete test identities. Tests exercise per-capability denial, foreground refusal, review/claim order, one execution, contradictory results, lost uploads unresolved SMS and uncertain contact-write replay, and enabled-policy selected-item/revision refusal before journal, claim or effect. Reply-draft automatic current-message behavior is tested but is not part of the explicit-review transition system.
bounds.limits: This is a finite TS boundary projection, not a machine-checked refinement or end-to-end native/provider proof. Concurrent independent coordinators, malformed principal/authentication handling, server durable claim atomicity, storage failures/lost commit acknowledgements, arbitrary restart and journal persistence, expiry and ledger-capacity exhaustion are outside the transition relation. Native Android permissions/roles, foreground/selected-item rechecks, native durable journals, device/carrier delivery and VVM provider availability remain separate qualification. The hook does not rebuild Gradle or claim physical-device acceptance. Read/body/transcript hard limits are rejected by the concrete validators; their byte domains are not enumerated in the model.
